name: Aadhaar / PAN identifier written to logs
attack_scenario: Logs aggregated to a SIEM, shipped to a third-party vendor, or left world-readable on disk leak millions of Aadhaar/PAN numbers; an insider or anyone with log access harvests them for identity theft, SIM-swap, and KYC fraud — a reportable breach under Indian law with no attacker skill required.
negative_test_hint: log a KYC verification record containing aadhaar number "123456789012" and assert the log output masks or omits the identifier instead of recording it in plaintext

exemplar.noncompliant: logger.info("KYC verified aadhaar_number=" + aadhaarNumber + " pan=" + panNo);
exemplar.explanation: India's Aadhaar Act 2016 (Sec. 29/37) and UIDAI/MeitY data-security regulations treat Aadhaar and PAN as regulated identifiers that must never land in plaintext application logs, which are readable by operators and often shipped to third-party SIEMs. Logging an opaque customer id keeps the audit trail useful without creating a reportable PII leak; masked, hashed, or tokenised forms of the identifier are equally safe.
